newsitem.title: UK: Britain says Indian undercarriage stowaway must go.
newsitem.headline: Britain says Indian undercarriage stowaway must go.

text.p: An Indian who miraculously survived as a stowaway in the frozen undercarriage of a jumbo jet flying from Delhi to London will not be allowed to remain in Britain.

Pardeep Saini, 23, endured temperatures as low as minus 60 C (-76F) during the flight last October, but his younger brother Vijay froze to death, his body falling to the ground as the jet's wheels were lowered for landing.
London's Evening Standard newspaper said on Tuesday that Saini's uncle Tarsem Singh has now received a letter from the British authorities rejecting his application for asylum.
Saini, a Sikh, had claimed he faced persecution in Punjab where he had been accused of supporting Sikh separatist extremists. He denied the charge.
A spokeswoman at the British Home Office said she could not confirm the Standard story since the interior ministry never commented on the outcome of asylum applications.
When Saini was found wandering on the tarmac at London's Heathrow airport in October, doctors said it was a miracle he had survived the harsh conditions of the flight.
They said he probably lost consciousness and went into a state of suspended animation which helped to prevent brain damage.
Piara Khabra, member of parliament for Southall, the area of west London where Saini has been living, called on Home Secretary Jack Straw to intervene in the case.
"Pardeep is clearly an amazing human being and deserves a chance," he told The Standard.
